name: RaycastUtils
src_typeComment: Shared raycast helpers — the exact "screen position -> world point" logic that was otherwise being hand-copied inline in several places across this toolkit (GridPlacer, TDTowerPlacer, and a couple of demo runners each wrote their own version). Pull new mouse/screen-picking code through here instead of re-deriving it again.

src_members.id: ScreenPointToWorld(Camera, Vector2, LayerMask, out RaycastHit, float)
src_members.sig: public static bool ScreenPointToWorld(Camera camera, Vector2 screenPoint, LayerMask layerMask, out RaycastHit hit, float maxDistance = 1000f)
src_members.name: ScreenPointToWorld
src_members.comment: The core operation: a screen-space point (usually Input.mousePosition) -> a real 3D hit against colliders on layerMask. Returns false (and a default hit) if nothing was hit or camera is null, rather than throwing — callers can just check the bool the same way Physics.Raycast itself works.

src_members.sig: public static bool MouseToWorld(Camera camera, LayerMask layerMask, out RaycastHit hit, float maxDistance = 1000f)
src_members.name: MouseToWorld
src_members.comment: Shortcut for the single most common case: raycasting from the CURRENT mouse position.

src_members.id: TryGetWorldPoint(Camera, Vector2, LayerMask, out Vector3, float)
src_members.sig: public static bool TryGetWorldPoint(Camera camera, Vector2 screenPoint, LayerMask layerMask, out Vector3 point, float maxDistance = 1000f)
src_members.name: TryGetWorldPoint
src_members.comment: Just the hit point, for callers that don't need the full RaycastHit (normal, collider, etc.).

src_members.sig: public static bool ScreenPointToPlane(Camera camera, Vector2 screenPoint, Plane plane, out Vector3 point)
src_members.name: ScreenPointToPlane
src_members.comment: A collider-free alternative — casts against a mathematical Plane instead of real geometry. Useful when there's no ground collider yet (prototyping) or the "ground" is meant to be an invisible fixed plane rather than real geometry — the same fallback technique Toolkit.EditorUtilities. MeasuringTapeWindow already uses for its own 2D mode.
